RagShortTexts: Lübeck presided as Queen of the Hanseatic League, dictating Baltic maritime trade through.

Variants.Content: Lübeck stood as the undisputed capital of the Hanseatic League, a city on the Trave whose merchants dominated the Baltic trade. Its ships and caravans carried salt from the Lüneburg saltworks, grain from the eastern estates and herring for the markets of the north, and these goods made the city rich beyond most German towns. Its municipal patricians drafted Lübeck Law, a codified body of town rights that more than a hundred merchant towns across the North Sea and Baltic adopted as their own. Brick Gothic churches rose along the river, and their stone towers marked the city for ships approaching from the sea.
The city's armed cog fleets enforced mercantile blockades against predatory princes, safeguarding autonomous burgher liberties.
